'''Mnggal-Mnggal''' was a [[Sentience/Legends|sentient]] entity known throughout the [[Unknown Regions/Legends|Unknown Regions]].

==Biography==
[[File:Mnggal-Mnggal_Host-TUR.jpg|thumb|left|200px|Mnggal-Mnggal prepares to take a [[Human/Legends|Human]] host.]]
Mnggal-Mnggal's origins were shrouded in mystery. It was a completely unique being, without analog even in [[Species/Legends|species]] catalogs as extensive as those of the [[University of Sanbra]]. It was believed by some, including the [[Chiss/Legends|Chiss]], to be extra-dimensional in origin, and comparisons were made to beings such as [[Waru]].<ref name="TUR">''[[The Unknown Regions]]''</ref><ref name="Danblog">{{Blogspot|subdomain=geekosity|url=2010/04/endnotes-for-star-wars-unknown-regions.html|name=Daniel Wallace's Geekosity|text=Endnotes for Star Wars: The Unknown Regions}}</ref> It was so ancient, at least by its own account, that it existed alongside the [[Celestial/Legends|Celestials]], and witnessed their sudden departure from [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]]. The [[Western barrier|hyperspace anomaly]] that bisected the galaxy, separating the highly populated portion of the galactic disk from the [[Unknown Regions/Legends|Unknown Regions]], was presumed by some to have been created by the powerful Celestials, possibly as a defensive measure against Mnggal-Mnggal and its infectious intentions.<ref name="TUR" />

Mnggal-Mnggal was a being composed solely of a thick gray ooze, able to move quickly and create a multitude of different forms. It was slimy to the touch and smelled of sweet rot. While it was a [[Changeling/Legends|shapeshifter]], it could not form the complex disguises of [[Species/Legends|species]] like the [[Shi'ido]], but its abilities were still versatile. It would form far-ranging pseudopods and eyestalks to explore or interact with others, or attack others with a fanged mouth. It could break its mass apart, spreading by creating [[Worm/Legends|worm]]-like forms, and was even able to fly by forming [[Bat/Legends|bat]]-like creatures.<ref name="TUR" />

Mnggal-Mnggal's most prolific&mdash;and deadly&mdash;form of movement, however, was by infecting and controlling other [[Sentience/Legends|sentient]] beings. While it could possess creatures, such as [[Nexu/Legends|nexu]] or [[Bantha/Legends|banthas]], Mnggal-Mnggal preferred sentients, and once a potential victim was in its sights, it went to work quickly. Once a being encountered a pool of Mnggal-Mnggal, the surface of the pool would explode outward, showering the being in droplets of the entity's body. The drops would then begin to slide toward the being's mouth and nostrils, but was also able to enter the body through the pores in a being's skin if need be. It would first penetrate the cranium and digest the [[Brain/Legends|brain]], then move on to the internal organs and tissues, increasing its mass all the while. It digested its victims from the inside out, filling every body part as it expanded and grew within the lifeless husk. Within twenty-four [[Standard hour/Legends|hours]], the victim was dead, filled entirely with Mnggal-Mnggal.<ref name="TUR" />

It could then fully control the victim's body, and was able to do so with enough precision to pilot vehicles. This was also how it obtained its sustenance, though it is unknown if the nutrients obtained were somehow spread throughout the being's myriad parts. A Mnggal-Mnggal-possessed [[Zombie/Legends|zombie]] could be easily distinguished from the body's former self. The possession was evidenced by a vacant gaze, a stiff-legged gait, and utter stillness when at rest. The victim's voice was also distorted, as Mnggal-Mnggal would have digested its vocal cords and lungs (or analogous organs) already; their voice would become buzzy and flat. Mnggal-Mnggal was not able to preserve its hosts, and after a [[Standard week/Legends|week]] they would begin to decay, with the entity's gray ooze slipping from their facial orifices. The zombies were also used to further infect others, by spewing Mnggal-Mnggal in the faces of new victims.<ref name="TUR" />

All parts of Mnggal-Mnggal, no matter what form or how far-flung across the galaxy, shared a single mind, which is what led others to classify the entity as a single being rather than a hive-minded species.<ref name="TUR" /><ref name="Danblog" />

At a long-forgotten point in the past, it had taken over and rendered lifeless the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] of [[Mugg Fallow]]. Eons later, Mnggal-Mnggal had spread so far across the planet, even filling its former oceans, that all that remained visible of the former world were barren continents and the remains of fossilized trees. Its "body" ran so far and deep across the planet that it ran in rivers across the continents and filled underground grottos. As testament to its depraved mind, Mnggal-Mnggal created a macabre decoration of a [[Fleet/Legends|fleet]] of derelict [[Starship/Legends|ships]] forming a ring around the planet, their origins ranging across millennia. Mnggal-Mnggal used its mind-controlled zombies to pilot the ships there, with [[Gree sailship]]s and a treasure barge once belonging to [[Xim/Legends|Xim the Despot]] among the lifeless fleet.<ref name="TUR" />

Over the course of its existence, Mnggal-Mnggal staked its claim to thousands of worlds, [[Moon/Legends|moons]], and [[Space station/Legends|space stations]] throughout the Unknown Regions, with infestations ranging from small pools in dark sewers to worlds ravaged and rendered as lifeless as Mugg Fallow.<ref name="TUR" />

As Mnggal-Mnggal spread throughout the Unknown Regions, some species native to the region opposed its incursions and sought to destroy the entity, knowing the extreme danger it posed. The [[Lugubraa]] and the [[Croke]] attempted to prevent any infestations within their territories, while the [[Chiss/Legends|Chiss]] took a more proactive stance. They not only possessed the most extensive collection of information on the entity in their great [[Expeditionary Library|data library]] on [[Csilla/Legends|Csilla]]&mdash;including the location of Mugg Fallow and all possible information on its origins&mdash;they also paid [[Bounty/Legends|bounties]] to any parties willing to attack infestations of Mnggal-Mnggal. The [[Viis Empire]] was decimated at one point by a Mnggal-Mnggal outbreak. Other violent outbreaks were responsible for similar power-changing events in the history of the Unknown Regions. On some primitive planets, it was worshiped by local tribes and known as the "rot god".<ref name="TUR" />

In later [[Standard year/Legends|years]], reports of Mnggal-Mnggal existed beyond the Unknown Regions, and it seemed as though it had managed to spread into [[Wild Space/Legends|Wild Space]] and even the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim Territories]]. During the reign of the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Empire]], some beings noted the similarities between Mnggal-Mnggal and the deadly plagues created by the Imperials' [[Imperial bioweapons Project I71A|Project Blackwing]].<ref name="TUR" />

==Personality and traits==
Mnggal-Mnggal desired nothing more than control, and subsequently sought to spread its body and influence over as many worlds as possible. If possible, it would destroy entire planets as it had with Mugg Fallow, but the idle amusement of [[Torture/Legends|torturing]] and [[Death/Legends|killing]] other sentients was entertaining as well.<ref name="TUR" />

Mnggal-Mnggal delighted in torturing and consuming other beings; indeed, it seemed to thrive more on beings' suffering than on the sustenance their bodies provided. Using its possession abilities, it would create torturous scenarios such as reuniting a grieving [[Parent/Legends|mother]] with the reanimated corpse of their [[Youngling/Legends|youngling]] time and time again. It would persuade other beings by playing with their emotions into making deadly decisions such as opening a ship's [[Airlock/Legends|airlocks]] or deactivating perimeter fences.<ref name="TUR" />

When conversing in its natural form, Mnggal-Mnggal spoke in dreamlike observations, often in verse, metaphors, and riddles. Due to its long life, it also spoke ancient [[Language/Legends|languages]] and conversed in long-forgotten conventions of speech. Though it told tales of the Celestials, [[Rakata/Legends|Rakata]], and the dawn of the [[Jedi Order/Legends|Jedi Order]], and seemed to know the current plots of galactic rulers, the locations of lost treasures, and the answers to age-old mysteries, some believed that every word it spoke was a lie.<ref name="TUR" />

==Behind the scenes==
{{Quote|Covan was the first to go, then Eelia. It's not taking me too. When I pull this trigger, that'll be the end of the Deep Charting Expedition.|From the log recorder of the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Republic]] scout ship ''[[Spotrunner]]'' {{C|cut content from ''[[The Unknown Regions]]''}}|<ref name="Danblog" />}}
This being was created for ''[[The Unknown Regions]]'' sourcebook. [[Daniel Wallace]] states that it was hinted that the Celestials created the hyperspace tangle surrounding the Unknown Regions to isolate themselves from Mnggal-Mnggal. The concept for the entity stems from [[Wikipedia:H. P. Lovecraft|H. P. Lovecraft]], and Daniel Wallace also states that the similarity between it and the infection in ''[[Death Troopers]]'' was unintentional. A last-minute addition included the line that tied Mnggal-Mnggal to Imperial Project Blackwing.

Furthermore, the entry's mention that Mnggal-Mnggal may have had extra-dimensional origins was confirmed by Wallace on his blog as a reference to Waru.<ref name="Danblog" />
